time_axis.history: monthly, Jan 2023 .. Jun 2026 (42 pts), index level base 100 = Jan 2023

value_semantics: index_series.value is an INDEX LEVEL (base 100), not a currency price. CommodityIndex.unit/currency cannot be filled from this source.

columns.name: .name
columns.full_name: .full — only present on the 17 flat-shape records

combos.csv.grain: one row per (formula, region) — the costing unit

columns.region: .region ("GL" assumed for flat records — see assumed_region)
columns.assumed_region: derived: true when the source stated no region
columns.variant: .variant — a grade of the same product in the same region (e.g. bentonite activated vs natural). Only 4 combos have one, and for those it is the only thing that tells the two rows apart, so do not key on formula+region.
columns.family: .family, falling back to the formula record
columns.subfamily: .subfamily, falling back to the formula record
columns.taxonomy_source: derived: combo | formula (which level supplied family/subfamily)
columns.weight_total: derived: sum of line weights (should be 100)
columns.w_unclassified: derived: weight of flags feedstock/idx (indexed, direct-vs-proxy not stated)
columns.priceable_pct: derived: share of TOTAL weight whose index resolves to a feed WITH a price series
columns.indexed_priceable_pct: derived: share of INDEXED weight that is priceable — 100% means this combo can be costed today; below that, some inputs have no series
columns.coverage_tier: derived: P1 all-direct | P2 some proxy | P3 proxy-heavy (>=50% of indexed weight), computed on indexed weight only
columns.loadable: derived: true when the combo has lines, a family, and 100% priceable indexed weight
columns.db_region: decision: decisions/region_basis.csv — the region name the database uses

combo_lines.csv.grain: one row per cost line — this is the bill of materials the costing engine needs

columns.weight_pct: line[0] as the source stores it (0-100)
columns.label: line[1]
columns.proxy_status: derived from raw_flag: direct | proxy | unclassified
columns.resolves_to: FCOVERED[type_code], or the type_code itself when it is already a feed slug
columns.resolution: derived: see _issues.csv — resolved | ambiguous | no_series | no_feed | unmapped | fixed
columns.label_short: derived: label truncated to 64 chars to fit FormulaComponent.label String(64). The full text stays in label.
columns.commodity_key: derived: resolves_to, validated against index_commodities.csv. Blank on fixed lines — FormulaComponent.commodity_id is nullable.

type_codes.csv.grain: one row per distinct type-code referenced by a line

columns.label: most common line[1] seen with this code
columns.proxy_status: derived: majority proxy_status of its lines
columns.ideal_index: PROXY_SWAP_REGISTRY.md — what we would rather have

index_commodities.csv.grain: one row per price series — this is the CommodityIndex load table. Distinct from index_feeds.csv, which is one row per card and can have several cards per series.

columns.display_name: INDEXES[slug].name for the first card reading this series
columns.source_region: the region the card states — note "multi" means no single region
columns.n_cards: derived: how many index cards read this series
columns.has_series: derived: whether a price history exists
columns.label_unit: unit parsed out of the region label — evidence, not the answer
columns.label_incoterm: Incoterm parsed out of the region label — evidence, not the answer
columns.label_named_place: named place parsed out of the region label — evidence, not the answer
columns.category: decision: decisions/index_basis.csv — a short token; INDEXES.cat is a display subtitle and will not fit CommodityIndex.category String(32)
columns.source_url: decision: decisions/index_basis.csv — no URL exists in either mockup
columns.value_kind: constant: index_level — base 100 = Jan 2023, NOT a currency price

index_feeds.csv.grain: one row per (feed_slug, region) — one index card as the app shows it. Note that several cards can share one underlying price series (e.g. naphtha, cbfs, pta and crude-oil all read "brent"), so series_key is NOT unique here.

columns.feed_key: derived: "<feed_slug>|<region>" — the unique key for this table
columns.series_key: INDEXES[slug].regKeys[region] — which price series this card reads
columns.shares_series_with: derived: other feed_slugs reading the same series (i.e. this card is a proxy view)
columns.name: .name (per-region override from ._regional when present)
columns.unit: parsed out of .regLabels[region] — e.g. "$/mt". Fills CommodityIndex.unit for the feeds whose label states one; blank where the label does not.
columns.source_note: the parenthetical in .regLabels[region] — the publishing agency / series id
columns.sourcing_note: INDEX_SOURCE_META[series_key].proxy — only populated for proxy feeds
columns.current_value: .currentVal — INDEX LEVEL, base 100 = Jan 2023, not a currency price
columns.volatility_pct: .volPct — only on the 38 feeds with the full intel block
columns.card_status: derived: full (rich intel block) | basic (card, no intel) | stub (no card at all — referenced by FCOVERED or FORE only)
columns.has_intel_block: derived: whether the mockup authored the rich card for this feed

columns.year: derived from position (IDX starts Jan 2023, FORE starts Jul 2026)

index_series_quarterly.csv.grain: one row per (series_key, year, quarter) — the grain index_values wants

columns.value: derived: mean of that quarter's monthly index levels

index_values.csv.grain: one row per (commodity, year, quarter) — actuals only. Matches the index_values table.

columns.value: derived: mean of that quarter's monthly index levels
columns.n_months: derived: how many months went into the mean

index_forecasts.csv.grain: one row per (commodity, year, quarter) — forecasts only. Kept separate because the index_values table has no actual-vs-forecast flag; loading these together would quietly turn a projection into history.

columns.value: derived: mean of that quarter's monthly forecast levels
